question: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is inscribed in circle \(\odot O\). Point \(A\) lies on the major arc \(BD\), and \(\angle BOD=140^\circ\). Find \(\angle C\) (in degrees).
solution: \(\angle A=\angle BOD\div 2=70^\circ\). Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so \(\angle C=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The opposite vertices \(A\) and \(C\) lie on opposite arcs with endpoints \(B,D\). Since \(A\) lies on the major arc \(BD\), \(C\) lies on the minor arc, so \(\angle C\) intercepts the major arc. This arc measures \(360^\circ-140^\circ=220^\circ\). By the inscribed angle theorem,
\[
\angle C=\frac{220^\circ}{2}=110^\circ.
\]
solutionMethods.label: Use the major arc directly

reference.question: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is inscribed in circle \(\odot O\). Point \(A\) lies on the major arc \(BD\), and \(\angle BOD=140^\circ\). Find \(\angle C\) (in degrees).
reference.solution:
Method 1: Find A and use opposite angles

\(\angle A=\angle BOD\div 2=70^\circ\). Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so \(\angle C=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ\).

Method 2: Use the major arc directly

The opposite vertices \(A\) and \(C\) lie on opposite arcs with endpoints \(B,D\). Since \(A\) lies on the major arc \(BD\), \(C\) lies on the minor arc, so \(\angle C\) intercepts the major arc. This arc measures \(360^\circ-140^\circ=220^\circ\). By the inscribed angle theorem,
\[
\angle C=\frac{220^\circ}{2}=110^\circ.
\]
